items.rationale: Honing realigns an edge that has bent over with use and removes almost no metal; sharpening grinds metal away to make a new edge. Thinking honing sharpens a dull knife is M12, and swapping the tools is M20.
A dull knife needs more force and slips off the food, so it cuts fingers more often than a sharp one. Believing a dull knife is safer is M11.

Honing is light, quick upkeep to do often; sharpening removes metal, so it is done only a few times a year. Sharpening constantly wears the knife away (M15), swapping the two shows M12, and washing alone never keeps an edge (M16).
Hand washing right away and drying protects the edge and the blade from rust, and soap removes food residue. Dishwashers knock and dull blades, and a soaking knife hides in the water and rusts.
A block, sheath or magnetic strip keeps the edge covered or held in place, so it neither dulls against other tools nor catches a hand. A loose knife in a drawer does both, which is M14.
If correct honing does not restore the bite, the edge has worn away rather than bent, so metal has to be removed by sharpening. Honing again would be M12.
